scope: Every numbered theorem-like environment of Sections 1 and 2 of diagonal-antidiagonal.tex; statements, their prose proofs (including the deferred proofs of Theorems 1.2 and 1.3), the named Lean declarations and the literature boundaries. This is a source review, not a kernel check.
snapshot_note: Assessment of the final tree. Ten of the eleven entries are formalised; Question 1.4 is open and recorded as a proposition. All three headline statements have complete proofs.

BoxLike.System.FraserBound.exact_statement: For the given finite nonempty contractive invertible box-like system S: packingDim S.attractor = upperBoxDim S.attractor and upperBoxDim S.attractor <= ofReal S.dimmaff. A theorem of the library: System.fraserBound_holds (BoxLike/Fraser/UpperBound.lean), along Fraser's proof, with no literature premise. Library statements that take it as a hypothesis receive this proof in Solution; no headline takes it.
BoxLike.System.FraserBound.verification: Read Theorem 2.3 and standing definitions in source. Source assumes at least two maps; Lean proves the single-map case separately. The first equality is proved separately (System.packingDim_attractor), so the content of the source beyond it is the inequality. The manuscript uses the upper Minkowski dimension, as the source does.
BoxLike.System.FraserBound.proof: Fraser's Section 5, "Upper bound (assuming no separation conditions)": his Lemma 5.1 (1) (FraserUpper.exists_sum_modSvfSum_le), the cover of X by the copies φ_𝐢(X) of the δ-stopping words and his bounds (5.7) and (5.8) for the projections give \overline{\dim}_M X ≤ dimmaff(X) (System.upperBoxDim_attractor_le_of_modPressure_neg, System.upperBoxDim_attractor_le_dimmaff); the equality \dim_P X = \overline{\dim}_M X is System.packingDim_attractor, and System.fraserBound_iff combines the two.

BoxLike.System.FraserROSC.exact_statement: For given finite nonempty S, RectangularOpenSet S implies packingDim, lowerBoxDim and upperBoxDim of the attractor all equal ofReal S.dimmaff. A theorem of the library: System.fraserROSC_holds (BoxLike/Fraser/Main.lean), along Fraser's proof, with no literature premise. BoxLike.System.FraserROSC.proof: Fraser's Section 5, "Lower bound (assuming the ROSC)": the open rectangles φ_𝐢(R), 𝐢 ∈ I_δ, are pairwise disjoint, a square of side 2δ meets boundedly many of them (System.fraserStopSum_meets_le), the projections onto the longer sides have the dimensions s(𝐢), and his Lemma 5.1 (2) (System.exists_le_fraserStopSum) bounds the stopped sums of ψ^t from below, which gives dimmaff(X) ≤ \underline{\dim}_M X (System.dimmaff_le_lowerBoxDim); with the first part (System.fraserROSC_of_fraserBound, System.fraserROSC_of_le). BoxLike.FraserJordanJurgaDecomposition.citation: Fraser-Jordan-Jurga, Lemma 1.3 and Corollaries 1.5 and 1.6, with Gibbs-measure existence on the mixing SFT as used in their setup
BoxLike.FraserJordanJurgaDecomposition.verification: Read setup at source lines 123-208 and the three cited results. Source uses positive entries and one-sided shifts. Absolute values, natural extension and axis symmetry justify the broader signed/two-sided formulation and extra decompositions. No separation condition is needed for the cited Section 1 assertions. Source-derived statement, not verbatim transcription.
BoxLike.FraserJordanJurgaDecomposition.gibbs_existence: The existence of the ergodic Gibbs measures on the mixing Sigma_Z is Bowen's theorem, which the library proves with no literature input (bowenGibbsExistence, existsUnique_ergodic_isGibbsPotential, BoxLike/Bowen/); the proof of the predicate starts from it (System.exists_isGibbs_potential₁).
BoxLike.FraserJordanJurgaDecomposition.proof: Bowen's theorem (bowenGibbsExistence) gives the ergodic Gibbs measure μ₁ for f_{1,s} on the mixing Σ_Z (System.exists_isGibbs_potential₁), and μ₂ is its image under the exchange of the axes (System.isGibbs_potential₂_map_flipAxis); the image of μ₁ under forgetting the axis has the Gibbs bounds of φ^s, since each word has two lifts and φ^s(A_w) is the larger of the two exponentials (System.hasGibbsBounds_map_unCode); every invariant measure with the Gibbs bounds equals this ergodic measure (System.eq_of_hasGibbsBounds); the four decompositions follow from Σ_Z = τ(Σ) ⊔ ω(Σ) and the exchange of the two ranges; the Lyapunov identities follow from Birkhoff's theorem along the two lifts and the relative-entropy comparison \overline{λ}(𝖠, μ₂) ≤ \overline{λ}(𝖠, μ₁) (System.lyapunov_map_unCode_of_isGibbs).

entries.label: thm:fraser
standing_hypotheses: Finite nonempty box-like contractive invertible affine IFS
ROSC for second and third conclusions
Both coordinate projections have Minkowski dimension one for third conclusion
entries.fidelity: All three assertions are proved for every box-like system, in the form of the source: \dim_P X = \overline{\dim}_M X ≤ dimmaff(X) (`System.fraserBound_holds`); under the rectangular open set condition \dim_P X = \dim_M X = dimmaff(X) (`System.fraserROSC_holds`; both parts, `paper_1_1_0`); and, if moreover both coordinate projections have Minkowski dimension one, dimmaff(X) = dimaff(X) (`paper_1_1_14`), so that \dim_P X = \dim_M X = dimaff(X) (`paper_1_1_13`). No literature premise is used. The box dimensions of the projections exist (`System.lowerBoxDim_coord_eq`). The upper Minkowski dimension of the manuscript is that of the source; without a separation condition the source asserts nothing about the lower Minkowski dimension.
proof_deviations: Proof: the paper cites Fraser with no proof; the formalisation follows Fraser's proof (arXiv:1108.2639v1, Section 5). The equality \dim_P X = \overline{\dim}_M X follows from bi-Lipschitz copies and Baire category, the argument Fraser quotes (`System.packingDim_attractor`). The upper bound \overline{\dim}_M X ≤ dimmaff(X) follows his "Upper bound (assuming no separation conditions)": his Lemma 5.1 (1) (`FraserUpper.exists_sum_modSvfSum_le`), the cover of X by the copies φ_𝐢(X) of the δ-stopping words and his bounds (5.7) and (5.8) for the projections (`System.upperBoxDim_attractor_le_of_modPressure_neg`, `System.upperBoxDim_attractor_le_dimmaff`). The lower bound dimmaff(X) ≤ \underline{\dim}_M X under the rectangular open set condition follows his "Lower bound (assuming the ROSC)": the open rectangles φ_𝐢(R), 𝐢 ∈ I_δ, are pairwise disjoint, a square of side 2δ meets boundedly many of them (`System.fraserStopSum_meets_le`), the projections onto the longer sides have the dimensions s(𝐢), and his Lemma 5.1 (2) (`System.exists_le_fraserStopSum`) bounds the stopped sums of ψ^t from below (`System.dimmaff_le_lowerBoxDim`). Fraser's Corollary 2.5 follows from the second part by equality of the singular value functions on [1, 2] (`System.FraserROSC.dimmaff_eq_dimaff`).

Deviation from Fraser's proof: in the super-multiplicative case t ≥ s_1 + s_2 of his Lemma 5.1 (2), the proof uses F(𝐢) = ∑_{m<b} ∑_{|𝐣|=m} ψ^t(𝐢𝐣), for a block length b with Ψ_b^t ≥ 1, in place of Fraser's k-block stopping set I_{k,δ}; F satisfies F(𝐢) ≤ ∑_j F(𝐢j) and is comparable with ψ^t (`System.exists_le_fraserStopSum_of_ge`). As Fraser writes it, I_{k,δ} need not be prefix-free, so his (5.5) needs a bounded-multiplicity argument that the formalisation does not use. This concerns Fraser's paper, not the manuscript.

entries.label: thm:box_like_sa
standing_hypotheses: a tuple of invertible matrices of operator norm less than one, the standing hypotheses of sec:box_like_self_affine.
entries.fidelity: the tuple statement is assembled (`box_like_sa_of_contracting`, and `PlanarSystem.box_like_sa` for the linear parts of a planar system): the tuple is box-like with rotations, A_i = D_i R_i with diagonal D_i and square isometries R_i of which at least one exchanges the axes and one does not, exactly when every A_i is diagonal or anti-diagonal and both types occur. `System.isBoxLikeWithRotations_iff` and `PlanarSystem.isBoxLikeWithRotations_iff_exists_system` identify the notion with `System.WithRotations`. "Rotating" is read as exchanging the coordinate axes, the convention of tex 644-647; under the reading "a rotation other than the identity" the lemma fails (−I is a diagonal rotation, the swap is an anti-diagonal reflection).
proof_deviations: Lean derives signed-permutation form from images of square corners and orthogonality; prose asserts images of e1,e2 lie among signed coordinate vectors. This supplies the omitted justification and is a minor proof reorganisation.

entries.label: thm:A_classification
standing_hypotheses: Arbitrary index type
Every matrix determinant nonzero
TupleProximal
entries.fidelity: Exact trichotomy, mutual exclusivity and both explanatory equivalences are proved, in greater generality than a finite tuple. Lines/vectors and equality/inclusion formulations are bridged internally. Proximality is essential for the second equivalence, and is present.
proof_deviations: Prose gives citations without a proof. Lean proves the claim directly: a finite invariant family consists of eigenlines of a proximal product (via powers and Cayley-Hamilton), then each generator preserves or swaps the two lines. No Barany-Kaenmaki-Rossi or Barany-Kaenmaki- Yu theorem is assumed.

entries.label: thm:box_like_proximal
standing_hypotheses: System S
S.Proximal
entries.fidelity: Conclusion is exactly a proximal diagonal generator in S or S.sq; rotations are not used, as in the prose.
proof_deviations: Proof: the prose argument (`System.Proximal.box_like_proximal`, the same statement as `hasProximalDiagonal_or_sq`). A proximal product B = A_w is diagonal with an even number of anti-diagonal factors. A diagonal factor with entries of distinct moduli is the generator. Otherwise |B| = c |B_1 B_2| ... |B_{2k-1} B_{2k}|, each B_{2i-1} B_{2i} is a diagonal matrix of A^2, and if all had entries of equal moduli, |B| would be scalar. `hasProximalDiagonal_or_sq`, which the rest of the library uses, is proved by this argument; the weighted-cocycle proof `hasProximalDiagonal_or_sq_of_cocycle` is an alternative.

entries.label: prop:ssc_no_overlap_not_pesc
standing_hypotheses: Only the displayed universal cited theorem premise
all construction parameters and all stated properties are produced in Lean
entries.fidelity: Exact four-map, three-diagonal/one-antidiagonal construction, proximality, irreducibility, failure of strong irreducibility, proximal diagonal generator, SSC, free full projective semigroup and failure of PESC. Lean also proves determinant sum<1. Freeness includes all words, not merely admissible orientation paths. The prose requests no transcendence of lambda; both endpoints take the source theorem `BaranyKaenmakiTheorem`.
proof_deviations: Proof: the prose argument (`NoOverlap.prop_ssc_no_overlap_not_pesc`, the same statement and premise as `ssc_no_overlap_not_pesc'`). The parameters lie outside the countable union of proper algebraic hypersurfaces over Q(λ,t) (Baire). Freeness goes through the multiplicative independence of λ, r_1..r_5, equal symbol counts and lengths, freeness of the conjugated three-map subsystem, the no-r coefficient of the translation variable of the first non-λ symbol and the remaining no-r terms, then cancellation and induction. The logarithmic limits appear as: for every c > 0, eventually Δ_n < c^n, which is what the last sentence of the proof uses. The sequential transcendental route (`exists_params`, `Params.freeProjective`) is a retained alternative and is not used by the endpoint.

cross_cutting_findings: Solution.lean has one PAPER_ENTRY per numbered item, aliasing the declarations that certify it with their exact types.
The source-level literature premises are conditional Prop arguments, not axioms. Formalisation completeness is distinguished from source fidelity and from assumed literature.
The question is open and is recorded as the proposition BoxLike.CoincidentProjectionDimensionsQuestion with explicit open status; no proof or answer is claimed.
The introduction distinguishes box-like tuples with both matrix types from all-anti-diagonal tuples, whose second iterates are diagonal. antiDiagonalExample shows why this distinction is needed.
